friend_2015_treadmill.citation: Kaminsky LA, Arena R, Myers J. Reference Standards for Cardiorespiratory Fitness Measured With Cardiopulmonary Exercise Testing: Data From the Fitness Registry and the Importance of Exercise National Database. Mayo Clin Proc. 2015;90(11):1515-1523. Table 3 (FRIEND rows).
friend_2015_treadmill.note: Directly measured treadmill VO2max (CPX, RER >= 1.00), apparently healthy US adults 20-79. A 2022 update (Mayo Clin Proc 97:285-293) reports treadmill values 1.5-4.6 mL/kg/min lower; its tables could not be accessed for verification, so the 2015 tables are used.

cooper_1968.citation: Cooper KH. A means of assessing maximal oxygen intake. Correlation between field and treadmill testing. JAMA. 1968;203(3):201-204.
cooper_1968.note: VO2max (mL/kg/min) = (distance in metres - 504.9) / 44.73. Derived in young men.

who_bmi_adults.citation: World Health Organization. Obesity and overweight (fact sheet), adults: overweight BMI >= 25, obesity BMI >= 30; WHO Global Database on BMI: normal range 18.50-24.99.
who_bmi_adults.note: Adult cut-offs. WHO uses BMI-for-age up to 19 years, so adult categories start at 20.

nice_ng246_whtr.citation: NICE guideline NG246 (2025), Overweight and obesity management: waist-to-height ratio 0.4-0.49 healthy central adiposity; 0.5-0.59 increased; 0.6 or more high.
nice_ng246_whtr.note: Adults with BMI under 35 kg/m2, both sexes and all ethnicities.

nhanes_rhr_2011.citation: Ostchega Y, Porter KS, Hughes J, Dillon CF, Nwankwo T. Resting pulse rate reference data for children, adolescents, and adults: United States, 1999-2008. National Health Statistics Reports no. 41. Hyattsville, MD: NCHS; 2011. Tables 2 and 3.
nhanes_rhr_2011.note: Seated radial pulse counted for 30 s and doubled, after about 4-5 minutes of rest; US population without conditions or medicines that affect the pulse. A lower pulse ranks higher here. Ages 12-79; the 80+ rows are incomplete in the source, so they are not used.

tveter_2014_sts.citation: Tveter AT, Dagfinrud H, Moseng T, Holm I. Health-related physical fitness measures: reference values and reference equations for use in clinical practice. Arch Phys Med Rehabil. 2014;95(7):1366-1373. Table 3 (30-s sit-to-stand).
tveter_2014_sts.note: Arms folded across the chest, chair 44-45 cm, 370 Norwegian adults 18-90. Under 50: 25.14 + 2.85 x sex; 50 and over: 50.61 - 0.36 x age - 0.10 x weight + 3.81 x sex (95% prediction interval +/-12.2 and +/-9.6). The percentile assumes a normal spread around the prediction.

strand_2014_plank.citation: Strand SL, Hjelm J, Shoepe TC, Fajardo MA. Norms for an isometric muscle endurance test. J Hum Kinet. 2014;40:93-102. Table 2.
strand_2014_plank.note: Forearm plank held to fatigue or loss of form, 471 US college students (mean age 20). Used for ages 17-25 only: no source with age-specific plank norms for older adults was found.

csep_path_pushups.citation: Canadian Society for Exercise Physiology (2019). CSEP Physical Activity Training for Health (CSEP-PATH) Resource Manual, 2nd ed. Push-up health benefit rating, as reprinted by ACE.
csep_path_pushups.note: Consecutive push-ups to fatigue, chest to a fist-height block. Men on toes, women on knees; other variants are not rated. Ages 15-69. Read from the ACE reprint, not the CSEP manual itself.

chms_2019_sit_reach.citation: Hoffmann MD, Colley RC, Doyon CY, Wong SL, Tomkinson GR, Lang JJ. Normative-referenced percentile values for physical fitness among Canadians. Health Reports. 2019;30(10):14-22. Table 3.
chms_2019_sit_reach.note: Canadian Health Measures Survey 2016-2017, CSEP sit-and-reach box. Our reach is measured from the toes; 26 cm is added to match the CSEP box, whose zero is 26 cm before the toes. Ages 14-69 used.

springer_2007_upst.citation: Springer BA, Marin R, Cyhan T, Roberts H, Gill NW. Normative values for the unipedal stance test with eyes open and closed. J Geriatr Phys Ther. 2007;30(1):8-15. Table 1.
springer_2007_upst.note: Eyes open, arms crossed on the chest, best of 3 trials capped at 45 s, 549 adults 18-99; no sex difference. Our test uses hands on hips and a 60 s cap, so the better leg is capped at 45 s and compared with the age group's mean and spread (the table's column says SE, but the values are SDs).

ymca_3min_step.citation: Golding LA, ed. YMCA Fitness Testing and Assessment Manual, 4th ed. Champaign, IL: Human Kinetics; 2000. 3-minute step test ratings, as reprinted by TotalWellness (2018).
ymca_3min_step.note: 30 cm (12 in) step, 24 steps a minute for 3 minutes, then seated; the score is the heart beats counted for one full minute starting 5 s after stepping. Ages 18 and over, by sex. Read from a reprint, not the manual itself.

marin_jimenez_2024_slj.citation: Marin-Jimenez N, et al. Eur J Sport Sci. 2024. doi:10.1002/ejsc.12182 [standing long jump reliability in adults, Adult-Fit]
marin_jimenez_2024_slj.note: Protocol: best of 2 jumps, two-foot take-off and landing, distance to the back of the nearest heel. Adults 18-64: ICC 0.94 without familiarisation (retest about 12 cm longer, MDC90 29 cm); after 3 practice sessions ICC 1.00. No adult age-by-sex norms were found, so results are self-comparison.

markovic_2004_jumps.citation: Markovic G, et al. J Strength Cond Res. 2004;18(3):551. doi:10.1519/1533-4287(2004)18<551:rafvos>2.0.co;2 [reliability of seven jump tests]
markovic_2004_jumps.note: Seven jump tests including the jump-and-reach (Sargent): Cronbach alpha 0.93-0.98, within-subject CV 2.4-4.6%. Jump-and-reach and flight-time heights differ, so one method is used throughout. Canadian adult norms exist (Payne et al. 2000) but their values could not be read; not used.

barrera_2025_505.citation: Barrera-Dominguez FJ, et al. Eur J Sport Sci. 2025. doi:10.1002/ejsc.12252 [505 change-of-direction test timed with a phone]
barrera_2025_505.note: 505: 10 m run-up (traditional) or standing start 5 m from the line (modified), 5 m in, 180-degree turn, 5 m out; slips and early turns discarded; 3 min rest. Phone video vs timing gates ICC >= 0.91. Hand stopwatch timing is less reliable (Chen 2021) and is flagged. No adult norms found.

haugen_buchheit_2016.citation: Haugen T, Buchheit M. Sports Med. 2016. doi:10.1007/s40279-015-0446-0 [sprint timing methods]
haugen_buchheit_2016.note: Manual timing should be avoided over 10-20 m because of large absolute errors; Kinetra therefore accepts only phone-video or timing-gate times for the sprint. No adult norms found.

eckner_2011_ruler_drop.citation: Eckner JT, Kutcher JS, Richardson JK. J Athl Train. 2011;46(4):409-414. doi:10.4085/1062-6050-46.4.409 [clinical reaction time, ruler-drop method]
eckner_2011_ruler_drop.note: Reaction time from the fall distance: t = sqrt(2d/g). Season-to-season ICC 0.65 (SEM 16.6 ms). With a plain ruler in adults 60+ reliability was lower (Ferreira 2024, ICC 0.57). Needs a helper. No adult norms found.

albrecht_2021_back_scratch.citation: Albrecht BM, Stalling I, Bammann K. BMC Geriatr. 2021. doi:10.1186/s12877-021-02188-9 [Senior Fitness Test percentiles, ages 65-75]
albrecht_2021_back_scratch.note: Back-scratch: one hand over the shoulder, the other up the back, distance between the middle fingers. Norms cover 65-75 (values not read) and Rikli & Jones 60-94; none under 60, so results are self-comparison.

plisky_2006_sebt.citation: Plisky PJ, et al. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther. 2006. doi:10.2519/jospt.2006.2244 [Star Excursion Balance Test and injury in high-school basketball]
plisky_2006_sebt.note: Players with an anterior reach difference above 4 cm were 2.5 times more likely to be injured. A 2021 meta-analysis (Plisky et al., IJSPT, PMC8486397) found this link in only 3 of 13 studies, so Kinetra shows the difference as a flag to look at, never as a risk score or a diagnosis.

munro_herrington_2011_hop.citation: Munro AG, Herrington LC. J Strength Cond Res. 2011. doi:10.1519/jsc.0b013e3181d83335 [between-session reliability of hop tests]
munro_herrington_2011_hop.note: Single-leg hop ICC 0.76-0.92 with a learning effect; all healthy subjects reached a limb symmetry index of at least 90%, which they recommend as a reference. The 90% figure comes from small and clinical samples and can overestimate function after knee injury (Wellsandt 2017): a flag only.

nacher_2026_isak_girths.citation: Nacher-Fernandez M, et al. J Int Soc Sports Nutr. 2026. doi:10.1080/15502783.2026.2724094 [ISAK girth measurement reliability]
nacher_2026_isak_girths.note: ISAK sites; each girth measured twice (a third time if they differ by more than 1%). Trained-measurer error about 0.6%; self-measurement reliability is unknown. Arm circumference tracked training change in young men (Gentil 2020). Population girth tables describe fat plus muscle, not muscle size, so results are self-comparison.

conley_1991_swim.citation: Conley DS, et al. Med Sci Sports Exerc. 1991. doi:10.1249/00005768-199106000-00019 [12-minute swim as a field test of peak aerobic power, men]
conley_1991_swim.note: Distance in 12 min correlated only r = 0.40 with peak aerobic power (0.42 in women, Conley 1992): a progress measure for swimmers, not a VO2 estimate. No norms or retest data were found.

hrr_step.description: 3-minute step test (30 cm step, 24 steps/min), then heart rate at 0, 60 and optionally 120 s.
hrr_step.title: HrrStepIn

pulls.description: Maximal consecutive pulling repetitions: overhand pull-ups, or inverted rows under a waist-high bar.
pulls.title: PullIn

sit_reach.description: Best of two reaches, in cm relative to the toes (0 = touching the toes, negative = short of them).
sit_reach.title: SitReachIn

single_leg_stance.description: Eyes open, hands on hips, up to 60 s per leg.
single_leg_stance.title: SingleLegStanceIn

broad_jump.description: Standing long jump: two jumps, both recorded; the best counts.
broad_jump.title: BroadJumpIn

vertical_jump.description: Jump-and-reach against a wall: standing reach, then the best of up to three jump reaches.
vertical_jump.title: VerticalJumpIn

agility_505.description: 505 change of direction, turning on each leg; times in seconds.
agility_505.title: Agility505In

sprint_20m.description: 20 m sprint from a standing start, 0.5 m behind the line. Hand timing is not accepted.
sprint_20m.title: Sprint20In

ruler_drop.description: Five recorded catches of a 60 cm ruler dropped by a helper; 61 = not caught.
ruler_drop.title: RulerDropIn

back_scratch.description: Distance between the middle fingers, cm: positive = overlap, negative = gap. Named by the top hand.
back_scratch.title: BackScratchIn

anterior_reach.description: Anterior reach on one leg along a tape line (Star Excursion style), best of 3 per stance leg.
anterior_reach.title: AnteriorReachIn

single_leg_hop.description: Single-leg hop for distance, best per leg, landing on the same leg.
single_leg_hop.title: SingleLegHopIn

circumferences.description: Girths in cm at ISAK sites, each the median of 2-3 measurements. Arms required, the rest optional.
circumferences.title: CircumferencesIn
